correctness.rationale: The binomial semigroup identity follows from Bernoulli survival composition. Gini coarea and the binomial column mass 1/p prove the first global bound. A monotone endpoint-column witness supplies an exact finite sum and the fixed-survival regime. A first-order affine rank-one operator has exact Gini norm p(n+1)(n+2)/6; the binomial tail remainder has an explicit bounded operator seminorm, proving the sharp late-time coefficient. Riemann sums give a strictly positive first-window lower envelope; the oscillation coefficient follows from the common zero atom and its exact pairwise equality. Finite exact-rational checks independently passed for all binary cuts through nine states, 2028 semigroup coefficient identities, and 12 Dobrushin cases. There are no unproved all-n finite maximizers or first-window limits.

value.rationale: The canonical independent-death Markov semigroup displays a quantitatively sharp two-stage nonnormal Gini transient: order-n amplification at log n time despite oscillation contraction, followed by a universal 1/6 late-window coefficient and stable-vs-amplifying boundary at 2log n -log6. The n/6 asymptotic disparity to the Dobrushin coefficient reveals metric-specific behavior not fixed by generic equivalence bounds. This is structurally motivated and extends beyond a routine isolated calculation.
